newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: National Mutual Funds NZ says Sept Qtr strong.
newsitem.headline: National Mutual Funds NZ says Sept Qtr strong.

text.p: National Mutual Funds Management NZ on Thursday reported strong investment results for the September quarter.
The balanced fund of the EFG Superannuation Fund of the NM superannuation scheme returned between 3.8 percent and 4.2 percent before tax for the quarter.
Returns ranged between 10.1 percent to 10.9 percent for the 12 months to September 30.
"The New Zealand asset classes really shone over the September quarter more than recovering the ground lost in the previous quarter," NMFM chief investment officer Barry Lindsay said.
"We certainly shared the concerns of many about the political scene leading up to the election and the persistence of inflation outside the target range," Lindsay said.
"However, we rationalised that most of these concerns seemed to have been factored into prevailing bond yields and share prices."
As a consequence, National Mutual's investment stance over the quarter was overweighted to New Zealand shares, underweighted cash but generally neutral to other asset classes, he said.
Property returned 6.4 percent before tax for the September quarter.
The outcome of Saturday's election was no surprise, Lindsay said.
"The general election result has not led us to review our current tactical strategy."

"While uncertainty over the results of the coalition discussions is not helpful in assessing the direction of the financial markets, the threat of a major shift in economic policy is not significant in our view."

NMFM reviewed their strategy at the beginning of October, with a slight increase in the already above neutral weighting in New Zealand shares and a little more invested in both New Zealand and International bonds, Linsday said.
"This meant that our client funds have participated well in the rally in the New Zealand markets this week," he said.
